newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Salvadoran bank executives arrested for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Salvadoran bank executives arrested for fraud.

text.p: Police on Wednesday said they arrested members of a private bank headed by one of El Salvador's top businessmen, accusing them of a massive fraud that bilked local investors of tens of millions of dollars.
But police did not name those arrested and judicial sources were unable to confirm whether Roberto Mathies Hill, a high-profile businessman closely tied to the ruling party, had been seized.
Mathies Hill's plush house in San Salvador was surrounded by police, and police ladders were propped against its high perimeter wall.
"There is nothing official," said Elena Miranda, spokeswoman for the Superintendency for Financial Institutions. "But I can't say it's not happening because everyone knows it is."
A police spokesman said more information on the scandal would be released on Thursday.
Mathies Hill is a member of a business group directly linked to the ruling Nationalist Republican Alliance (ARENA). He is also head of the country's football selection committee.

Scores of furious investors lined up at his financial firm, known as Finsepro, after local media circulated reports of the fraud. According to the reports, the accused are charged with embezzling between $30 million to $90 million from investment accounts at Finsepro.
